description: Expert mathematical roadmap; all original Lean blocks are uncompiled pseudocode and are intentionally excluded.

nodes.title: Normalized convex-containment count
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF p. 8
nodes.statement:
A finite multi-family $\mathcal S$ satisfies the convex Wolff axiom with error $A$ if
\[\#\{S\in\mathcal S:S\subset W\}\le A|W|\#\mathcal S\quad(W\text{ convex}).\]
For a tube family this implies $\#\mathcal T\gtrsim A^{-1}\delta^{-2}$ by testing $W=T$.
No upper bound $\#\mathcal T\lesssim\delta^{-2}$ is imposed.
nodes.note: Interface note. The normalization is by the whole family cardinality. It differs from the traditional cardinality-normalized Wolff axiom. Tube volumes and the bounded ambient chart are kept explicit.

nodes.title: Geometric and shaded unit rescaling
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF pp. 8, 38; WZ1 Definition 3.2
nodes.statement:
For a convex parent $U$, map its circumscribed John ellipsoid to the unit ball by $\phi_U$.
For structural tube arguments use the compatible shaded rescaling from WZ2 Section 6.1: rotate the parent axis to $e_3$, dilate transverse coordinates by $\rho^{-1}$, and re-cubulate at $\delta/\rho$.
The two choices differ by bounded normalizations; in dimension three the volume Jacobian is comparable to $\rho^{-2}$.

nodes.title: Convex Wolff axioms at every scale
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF p. 9
nodes.statement:
The tubes are essentially distinct. For every $\rho_0\in[\delta,1]$, there are $\rho\in[\rho_0,A\rho_0)$ and $\rho$-tubes $\mathcal T_\rho$ such that:
(i) $\mathcal T_\rho$ is an $A$-uniform partitioning cover of $\mathcal T$;
(ii) for each parent, the unit-rescaled child family satisfies the convex Wolff axiom with error $A$.
This is the root hypothesis; neither a direction-separated cover nor self-similar child counts is stipulated.

nodes.title: Coarse and fine multi-scale inheritance
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF pp. 9-10
nodes.statement:
If $\mathcal T$ satisfies the multi-scale convex Wolff axiom with error $A$, then for every $\rho_0\in[\delta,1]$ one can choose $\rho\in[\rho_0,A\rho_0]$ and a $\rho$-cover whose coarse family and every unit-rescaled child family satisfy the same multi-scale condition with error $O(A)$.
Partitioning forces the child-incidence clusters at successive scales to form a nested tree.

nodes.title: The counterexample deficit sigma_CW
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF p. 38
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathsf{Bad}(s)$ mean: for every $\eta,\delta_0>0$, some $0<\delta\le\delta_0$ has multi-scale convex Wolff error $\delta^{-\eta}$, shading density $\delta^\eta$, and $|E_C|\le\delta^s$.
Define $\sigma=\sigma_{\rm CW}=\sup(\{0\}\cup\{s>0:\mathsf{Bad}(s)\})$.
Failure of Theorem 5.2 gives $\sigma>0$. This is a new deficit for a different admissible class, not WZ1's $\sigma_3$.

nodes.title: Definition of epsilon-CW-extremal
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF p. 39
nodes.statement:
Write $E_C=\bigcup_TY(T)$ and $\sigma=\sigma_{\rm CW}$. The pair $C=(\mathcal T,Y)_\delta$ is \emph{$\varepsilon$-CW-extremal} precisely when
\[\begin{aligned}
&\mathcal T\text{ satisfies multi-scale convex Wolff with error }\delta^{-\varepsilon},\\
&\sum_T|Y(T)|\ge\delta^\varepsilon\sum_T|T|,\\
&|E_C|\le\delta^{\sigma-\varepsilon}.
\end{aligned}\]
This is WZ2 Definition 6.1, where it is called $\varepsilon$-extremal. The added CW label distinguishes it from WZ1's different extremal class.
nodes.note: Interface note. All epsilon-CW-extremal labels in this atlas refer to these three conditions. The shading density is an average relative to total tube volume; it is not a requirement on every individual tube.

nodes.title: Extremizers exist at arbitrarily small scales
nodes.source: WZ2 paragraph after Definition 6.1, PDF p. 39
nodes.statement:
In the contradiction regime $\sigma>0$, for every $\varepsilon,\delta_0>0$ there is an $\varepsilon$-extremal pair at some $0<\delta\le\delta_0$.
Choose a bad exponent greater than $\sigma-\varepsilon$ and use the defining arbitrarily-small-scale witness.
The scale is existential, not prescribed.

nodes.title: Balanced extremal coarse and fine families
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF pp. 39-40; replaces WZ1 Proposition 3.2
nodes.statement:
For every $\varepsilon>0$ choose $\eta,\delta_0>0$.
If $C$ is $\eta$-extremal and $\delta^{1-\varepsilon}\le\rho\le\delta^\varepsilon$, there are a refinement $C'$ and a balanced $\rho$-cover $D$ such that $D$ and each unit-rescaled child family are $\varepsilon$-extremal.
For every point $p$,
\[\begin{split}\#\mathcal T_D(p)&\le\rho^{2-\sigma-\varepsilon}\#\mathcal T_D,\\
\#\mathcal T_{C'}[U](p)&\le(\delta/\rho)^{2-\sigma-\varepsilon}\#\mathcal T_{C'}[U].\end{split}\]
The fine/coarse product comparison also supplies matching lower multiplicity estimates with a reserved small loss.

nodes.title: Local rescaling and multiplicity control
nodes.source: WZ1 Lemma 3.3, pp. 13-14; normalized CW form in the proof of WZ2 Proposition 6.2
nodes.statement:
For an admissible unit-rescaled child family at mesh $s=\delta/\rho$, apply the WZ2 deficit lower-envelope estimate to its constant-multiplicity refinement.
Since its total shading mass is at most $O(s^2\#\mathcal T_{\rm child})$ and its union has volume at least $s^{\sigma+\varepsilon}$, its multiplicity obeys
\[\mu_{\rm fine}\lesssim s^{2-\sigma-\varepsilon}\#\mathcal T_{\rm child}.\]
The rescaled family must satisfy the multi-scale convex Wolff condition and retain the stipulated density; Lemma 2.13 and cover rebuilding supply these hypotheses.
nodes.note: Interface note. This is the transferred proof interface, not the literal WZ1 formula (rho/delta)^(sigma_n+epsilon). WZ2 may have many more than delta^(-2) tubes, so the normalized tube count must remain visible.

nodes.title: Robust transversality
nodes.source: WZ1 Lemma 3.4, pp. 17-18; WZ2 Proposition 6.2 supplies its CW input
nodes.statement:
For every small $\theta>0$, a sufficiently CW-extremal configuration admits a refinement with robust angular transversality.
In normalized counting form, at every shaded point $p$ and unit vector $v$,
\[\#\{T\in\mathcal T(p):\angle(v,\operatorname{dir}T)<\delta^\theta\}
\lesssim\delta^{2-\sigma+\theta\sigma/2}\#\mathcal T.\]
Use a partitioning $\delta^\theta$-cover and the fine multiplicity bound from Proposition 6.2; the participating tubes occupy $O(1)$ parents.
nodes.note: Interface note. Constants and the small margin are absorbed by the eta/theta hierarchy. This angular-incidence conclusion does not say that the full tube family has separated directions.

nodes.title: Mild anisotropic rescaling preserves extremality
nodes.source: WZ1 Lemma 3.5, p. 18; CW transfer used by WZ2 Sections 6.3-6.4
nodes.statement:
Restrict a CW-extremal configuration to a prism retaining a stipulated small-power fraction of its shading mass.
Transport by a translation and diagonal dilation with all singular values between $\delta^\eta$ and $\delta^{-\eta}$.
After re-cubulation, removal of bounded multiplicities and rebuilding the cover witnesses, the transported family is $\varepsilon$-CW-extremal at a comparable power scale $\delta\le s\le\delta^{1-O(\eta)}$.
The density and convex-containment errors incur $\delta^{-O(\eta)}$ losses.
nodes.note: Interface note. The old absolute mass threshold and automatic sticky-subfamily observation are replaced by density relative to total tube volume and explicit multi-scale cover reconstruction. This is the transport interface implicit in the author-endorsed WZ2 transfer, not a new independent black-box theorem.

nodes.title: The multi-scale convex Wolff deficit is zero
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF pp. 43-44
nodes.statement:
If $\sigma>0$, apply the lower bound with exponent $\sigma/4$.
Choose the small-image construction with loss $\kappa<\sigma/4$ and $\kappa$ smaller than the lower-bound admissibility threshold.
At arbitrarily small mesh the same pair obeys
$\delta^{\sigma/4}\le |X_f(C)|\lesssim\delta^{\sigma-\kappa}$,
which is impossible. Therefore $\sigma_{\rm CW}=0$.

nodes.title: Discrete union estimate for multi-scale convex Wolff tubes
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF p. 35; proof in Sections 6-7
nodes.statement:
For every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $\eta,\delta_0>0$ such that for every $0<\delta\le\delta_0$:
if $\mathcal T$ satisfies the convex Wolff axioms at every scale with error $\delta^{-\eta}$ and $Y$ is $\delta^\eta$-dense, then
\[\left|\bigcup_{T\in\mathcal T}Y(T)\right|\ge\delta^\varepsilon.\]
This is the sole root theorem. No Hausdorff/Assouad-dimension deduction is part of the graph.

nodes.title: Plane map
nodes.source: WZ2 Section 6.1, PDF p. 38; WZ1 Definition 4.1
nodes.statement:
A plane map $V:E_C\to S^2$ satisfies $|\operatorname{dir}(T)\cdot V(x)|\le\delta$ for every shaded incidence $x\in Y(T)$.
The normal determines the plane $V(x)^\perp$. For Lipschitz statements, use a consistently oriented normal on the selected chart, or retain a projective-plane metric.
nodes.note: Interface note. Changing the sign of a normal does not change its plane. An implementation should state explicitly which orientation convention is used when taking |V(p)-V(q)|.

nodes.title: Endpoint multilinear Kakeya input
nodes.statement:
For a finite family of $\delta$-tubes in $\mathbb R^3$ with unit directions $v_T$,
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^3}\left(\sum_{T_1,T_2,T_3}
1_{T_1}1_{T_2}1_{T_3}\,|\det(v_{T_1},v_{T_2},v_{T_3})|\right)^{1/2}
\lesssim(\delta^2\#\mathcal T)^{3/2}.
\]
The implicit constant is absolute in the normalized tube geometry.
nodes.note: Interface note. This theorem is an imported analytic black box. The determinant is the volume of the parallelepiped, despite the source's descriptive word 'area'.

nodes.title: Weak planiness
nodes.source: WZ1: (4.3), pp. 19-20; CW configuration transfer: WZ2 Sections 6.2-6.3
nodes.statement:
There are $\eta,\delta_0>0$ such that every $\eta$-CW-extremal configuration in $\mathbb R^3$ at $0<\delta\le\delta_0$ has a refinement $C'$ and a unit-normal map $V$ with
$|V(x)\cdot\operatorname{dir}(T)|\le\delta^{\sigma/2}$ for all shaded incidences of $C'$.
Here $\sigma=\sigma_{\rm CW}$ is the WZ2 deficit.
nodes.note: Interface note. CW transfer check: retain W=delta^2 #T in the multilinear bound and mu approximately delta^(-sigma) W. The factors W^(3/2) cancel in the broad-set estimate. Robust angular incidence bounds are supplied by the CW version of Lemma 3.4. Shading selection retains a fixed incidence fraction; no absolute upper tube count is used.

nodes.title: Coarsen weak planiness to a plane map
nodes.source: WZ1: (4.10), pp. 20-21; CW configuration transfer: WZ2 Sections 6.2-6.3
nodes.statement:
For each $\varepsilon>0$, sufficiently extremal $C$ and $\rho\in[\delta^{1-\varepsilon},\delta^\varepsilon]$ with $|V(x)\cdot\operatorname{dir}T|\le\rho/2$ admit a refinement $C'$ and an $\varepsilon$-extremal $\rho$-cover $D$ with plane map $\widetilde V$.
The map $\widetilde V$ is constant on $\rho$-cubes and equals some original value $V(p_Q)$ in each occupied cube.
nodes.note: Interface note. CW transfer check: with child count k and parent count N_rho, #T approximately k N_rho. The associated-parent fraction is bounded below by mu_delta/(mu_fine mu_coarse), a small-power quantity by Proposition 6.2. Pullback uses the parent/cube incidence-mass balance built during its proof. Direction comparison then gives rho/2+rho/2.

nodes.title: Small oscillation on a fixed cube scale
nodes.source: WZ1: pp. 21-22; CW configuration transfer: WZ2 Sections 6.2-6.3
nodes.statement:
For every $\varepsilon>0$, sufficiently extremal $C$ with plane map $V$ and middle scale $\rho$ has an $\varepsilon$-CW-extremal subcollection $C'$ such that
$|V(p)-V(q)|\le\rho$ whenever $p,q\in E_{C'}$ lie in a common $\rho$-cube.
nodes.note: Interface note. CW transfer check: transverse fine pairs number approximately mu_delta^2. Dividing by mu_fine^2 and comparing with mu_coarse^2 leaves (mu_delta/(mu_fine mu_coarse))^2; the tube counts cancel. A fixed transverse parent pair determines a normal up to sign. Cap pigeonholing absorbs the small angular loss while retaining incidence mass.

nodes.title: Small oscillation for nearby points
nodes.source: WZ1: p. 22; CW configuration transfer: WZ2 Sections 6.2-6.3
nodes.statement:
Under the same hypotheses, an $\varepsilon$-CW-extremal subcollection satisfies
$|p-q|\le\rho\Longrightarrow |V(p)-V(q)|\le2\rho$ on its union.
The proof discards a constant fraction of coarse cubes to enforce separation.
nodes.note: Interface note. CW transfer check: colour the coarse cubes and retain the colour carrying the largest incidence mass. This is a fixed-factor shading restriction. Keep the underlying tube family, including tubes with empty shading, so its multi-scale CW property is unchanged.

nodes.title: Iterate to a Lipschitz plane map
nodes.source: WZ1: pp. 22-23; CW configuration transfer: WZ2 Sections 6.2-6.3
nodes.statement:
A sufficiently CW-extremal configuration whose plane map $V$ is constant on $\delta$-cubes has an $\varepsilon$-CW-extremal subcollection on which $V$ is $\delta^{-\varepsilon}$-Lipschitz.
This iterates Corollary 4.6 at finitely many power scales.
nodes.note: Interface note. CW transfer check: only finitely many power scales delta^(j/N) are used. Their mass-retention exponents add; choose their sum below the final density budget. The geometric interpolation gives Lip(V) at most 2 delta^(-1/N). Tube counts do not enter this interpolation.

nodes.title: Existence of Lipschitz plane data
nodes.source: WZ1: p. 23; CW configuration transfer: WZ2 Sections 6.2-6.3
nodes.statement:
For every $\varepsilon,\delta_0>0$, some $0<\delta\le\delta_0$ admits an $\varepsilon$-CW-extremal configuration with a $\delta^{-\varepsilon}$-Lipschitz plane map.
Assemble extremizer existence, weak planiness, coarsening and Lipschitz refinement, using WZ2 Proposition 6.2 throughout.
nodes.note: Interface note. CW transfer check: use extremizer existence from WZ2 Section 6.2, weak planiness, and Proposition 6.2 at a coarse mesh comparable to delta^(sigma/2). Apply the finite Lipschitz refinement and rename the resulting mesh. Sigma is sigma_CW throughout.

nodes.title: Upper AD covering condition
nodes.source: WZ2 Section 6.1, PDF p. 38; WZ1 Definition 4.2
nodes.statement:
For $E\subset\mathbb R$, the condition $(\delta,\alpha,A)_1$-ADset means
$\mathcal E_\rho(E\cap I)\le A(r/\rho)^\alpha$ for every $\rho\ge\delta$ and interval $I$ of length $r\ge\rho$.
Only an upper covering bound is required. It passes to arbitrary subsets.
The higher-dimensional ball version from WZ1 is used within its Section 8 projection argument.
nodes.note: Interface note. This is the convention recalled in WZ2, not two-sided classical AD regularity. Keep it distinct from normalized Frostman sets and absolute Katz-Tao sets.

nodes.title: Grain count in tau-cubes
nodes.source: WZ1: (4.15), pp. 23-25; CW configuration transfer: WZ2 Sections 6.2-6.3
nodes.statement:
For sufficiently CW-extremal $C$ with a $\delta^{-\eta}$-Lipschitz plane map, $\rho\in[\delta^{1-\varepsilon},\delta^\varepsilon]$ and $\tau\in[\rho^{1-\varepsilon},\rho^{1/2}]$, an $\varepsilon$-CW-extremal subcollection $C'$ satisfies
$\mathcal E_\rho(V(Q)\cdot(E_{C'}\cap Q))\le\rho^{-\varepsilon}(\tau/\rho)^{1-\sigma}$
for every $\tau$-cube $Q$. Here $V(Q)$ is evaluated at its centre using the chosen extension.
nodes.note: Interface note. The proof's Córdoba-type L2 estimate is elementary tube-intersection geometry and Cauchy-Schwarz. It is not a separate imported Córdoba theorem. CW transfer check: balanced union volumes give |E_rho intersection Q_tau| approximately tau^3 |E_rho|/|E_tau|, hence at most a small loss times rho^sigma tau^(3-sigma). The elementary Córdoba argument fills each grain to a small-power fraction of rho tau^2. Their quotient is (tau/rho)^(1-sigma). Robust transverse companions replace any direction-separation inference.

nodes.title: Grain count in thin prisms
nodes.source: WZ1: (4.20), pp. 26-28; CW configuration transfer: WZ2 Sections 6.2-6.3
nodes.statement:
Under the same scale and plane-map hypotheses, an $\varepsilon$-CW-extremal subcollection satisfies:
for every $\rho^{1/2}$-cube $Q$, put $F_Q=V(Q)\cdot(E_{C'}\cap Q)$.
For each interval $J$ of length $\tau$,
$\mathcal E_\rho(J\cap F_Q)\le\rho^{-\varepsilon}(\tau/\rho)^{1-\sigma}$.
This is a localized interval bound, stronger than only counting the entire projection.
nodes.note: Interface note. CW transfer check: for R=sqrt(rho), the balanced volume per R-cube is approximately rho^((sigma+3)/2). A grain has volume rho^2. Use the Fubini line bound |L intersection E_Q| at least a constant times |E_Q|/rho, then popular grains hit by L retain a small-power fraction of E_Q. Coarse restrictions pull back through parent/cube incidence-mass balance.

nodes.title: Fixed-mesh spacing at one grain scale
nodes.source: WZ1: pp. 28-29; CW configuration transfer: WZ2 Sections 6.2-6.3
nodes.statement:
For sufficiently extremal $C$ with a Lipschitz plane map and a middle scale $\rho$, an $\varepsilon$-CW-extremal subcollection $C'$ satisfies, for each $\rho^{1/2}$-cube $Q$ and each interval $J$ with $|J|\ge\rho$,
\[\mathcal E_\rho\!\left(J\cap V(Q)\cdot(E_{C'}\cap Q)\right)
\le\delta^{-\varepsilon}(|J|/\rho)^{1-\sigma}.\]
This is a fixed covering-mesh estimate. Iterate in the covering mesh, as in Lemma 4.12, before asserting the full ADset condition.
nodes.note: Interface note. Checked interface: iteration in the interval-length parameter gives the displayed fixed-covering-mesh estimate. It alone does not imply an ADset bound at every larger covering mesh. This card is intentionally narrowed to the bound used by Lemma 4.12; that subsequent mesh iteration supplies the full AD conclusion. CW transfer uses shading-mass budgets and Proposition 6.2.

nodes.title: AD spacing at every grain scale
nodes.source: WZ1: (4.29), pp. 29-30; CW configuration transfer: WZ2 Sections 6.2-6.3
nodes.statement:
For sufficiently extremal $C$ with a $\delta^{-\eta}$-Lipschitz plane map, an $\varepsilon$-CW-extremal subcollection satisfies:
$V(p)\cdot(E_{C'}\cap B(p,\rho^{1/2}))$ is a $(\rho,1-\sigma,\delta^{-\varepsilon})_1$-ADset for all $\rho\in[\delta,1]$ and all centres $p$.
Iterate Lemma 4.11 over $\rho$, then compare intervening scales. First obtain the fixed-mesh bound for every $r$. For $r\ge\rho$, use $B(p,\sqrt\rho)\subset B(p,\sqrt r)$ to control the $r$-covering number of the smaller projected grain; this supplies all covering meshes in the AD definition.
nodes.note: Interface note. Plane values outside the union need an explicit extension or a harmless centre-selection convention. The original exposition suppresses this domain bookkeeping. CW transfer check: iterate the fixed-mesh output of Lemma 4.11 in the grain mesh and interpolate intervening power scales. Once the fixed-mesh bound holds at every r, B(p,sqrt(rho)) is contained in B(p,sqrt(r)) for r>=rho, giving the full ADset condition. Extend the plane values or fix centre witnesses explicitly. All selections retain controlled shading mass.

nodes.title: Global and local grains with Lipschitz data
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF p. 40; transferred WZ1 Proposition 4.1
nodes.note: Interface note. The entire WZ1 Section 4 proof is expanded in the plane and grain views. Proposition 6.2 replaces Proposition 3.2; numerical multiplicities are normalized by cardinality.

nodes.title: Vertical trapezoids and parents
nodes.statement:
A vertical trapezoid is $R=\{(z,t):z\in J,\ |t-L(z)|\le s\}$, with affine centre line $L$.
Its length is $|J|$, height is $s$, and slope is the slope of $L$.
Across scales, a parent relation means geometric containment of the child trapezoid in the unique parent.

nodes.title: Why the expansion alternative is impossible
nodes.source: WZ1: Proof of Lemma 5.3, p. 37; discussion p. 5
nodes.statement:
If $A$ is an $(r_0,1-\sigma,C)$-ADset, then for $\rho\ge r_0$ and $R=|I|/\rho$,
$\mathcal E_\rho(A\cap I)\le C R^{1-\sigma}$.
An expansion lower bound $\mathcal E_\rho(A\cap I)\ge R^{1-\varepsilon}$ forces $R^{\sigma-\varepsilon}\le C$.
Choose $\varepsilon<\sigma$ and make the permitted interval-to-scale ratio exceed this threshold.
nodes.note: Interface note. The direct proof is an exponent comparison. The introduction attributes a related observation to [12, Proposition 6.13]; that citation is not invoked as a separate black box in the written proof of Lemma 5.3.

nodes.title: Dot-product expansion or orthogonal lines
nodes.source: WZ1: (5.1)-(5.2), p. 32; proof Section 8
nodes.statement:
For every $\varepsilon>0$, choose $\eta,\delta_0>0$.
For $(\delta,1,\delta^{-\eta})$-ADsets $F,G\subset[0,1]^2$, either
(A) an affine line $\ell$ and the orthogonal line $\ell^\perp$ through the origin have
$\mathcal E_\delta(F\cap N_\delta\ell),\mathcal E_\delta(G\cap N_\delta\ell^\perp)\ge\delta^{\varepsilon-1}$; or
(B) for every $H\subset F\times G\times G$ with $\mathcal E_\delta(H)\ge\delta^{\eta-3}$, some $\rho\ge\delta$ and interval $I$, $|I|\ge\delta^{-\eta}\rho$, satisfy
$\mathcal E_\rho(I\cap\{a\cdot(b_1-b_2):(a,b_1,b_2)\in H\})\ge(|I|/\rho)^{1-\varepsilon}$.
nodes.note: Interface note. The second alternative is universal in H. It is not the weaker assertion that a specially selected H expands.

nodes.title: Local linearity from the two grain structures
nodes.source: WZ1: (5.3)-(5.4), pp. 33-38; CW configuration transfer: WZ2 Sections 6.2-6.3
nodes.statement:
For suitable $\eta,\rho_0$, let $I$ have length $\rho^{1/2}$, $Z\subset I$, and let $f:I\to[0,1]$ and $V:E\to S^2$ be $1$-Lipschitz.
Assume $E\subset[-1,1]^2\times Z$ is a $\rho$-cube union lying in a $\rho^{1/2}$-neighbourhood of a line with direction $(-f(z_*),1,0)$, and $|E|\ge\rho^{1+\sigma/2+\eta}$.
Assume $|V\cdot e_3|\le1/2$, the global slice images are $(\rho,1-\sigma,\rho^{-\eta})_1$-ADsets, and
$|V(p)\cdot(E\cap B(p,\rho^{1/2}))|\le\rho^{(1+\sigma)/2-\eta}$.
Then an affine function $L:I\to[0,1]$ and $Z_{\rm lin}\subset Z$ satisfy
$|Z_{\rm lin}|\ge\rho^{1/2+\varepsilon}$ and $|f(z)-L(z)|\le\rho$ on $Z_{\rm lin}$.
nodes.note: Interface note. LocalLinearityHyp is exactly the preceding hypothesis list. The proof encodes closed grain paths as dot products, applies Theorem 5.2, and rules out expansion by the AD exponent gap.

nodes.title: Piecewise linear approximation at one scale
nodes.source: WZ1: pp. 38-39; CW configuration transfer: WZ2 Sections 6.2-6.3
nodes.statement:
For a sufficiently CW-extremal configuration with the two grain properties of Proposition 4.1 and middle scale $\rho$, there are an $\varepsilon$-CW-extremal subcollection $C'$ and a $2$-Lipschitz function $L$.
The function $L$ is affine on each interval $[k\rho^{1/2},(k+1)\rho^{1/2}]$ and satisfies
$|f(z)-L(z)|\le\rho$ for $z\in\pi_z(E_{C'})$.
nodes.note: Interface note. CW transfer check: heavy parent/cube incidences give vertical support of length at least a small-power fraction of rho, so averaging the fine global AD counts transfers them to the coarse shading. Balanced R=sqrt(rho) cubes have volume approximately rho^((sigma+3)/2); a popular fine rectangle meets approximately R^(-1) such cubes, producing the rho^(1+sigma/2) region required by Lemma 5.3. Work on popular heights before converting height retention into shading mass.

nodes.title: Compatible approximations at many scales
nodes.source: WZ1: pp. 39-40; CW configuration transfer: WZ2 Sections 6.2-6.3
nodes.statement:
For $\varepsilon>0$ and integer $N\ge1$, let $\rho_j=\delta^{j/N}$.
A sufficiently CW-extremal configuration with Proposition 4.1 data has an $\varepsilon$-CW-extremal subcollection and functions $L_j$, each $2$-Lipschitz and affine on intervals of length $\rho_j^{1/2}$, with $|f-L_j|\le\rho_j$ on $D=\pi_z(E_{C'})$.
The subsequent refinement on p.~40 also ensures each occupied interval has $|I\cap D|\ge4^{-N}\delta^\varepsilon |I|$, and occupied intervals are non-adjacent at each scale.
nodes.note: Interface note. The popularity and separation conclusions are the explicit unnumbered refinement after Lemma 5.5; Corollary 5.6 uses this strengthened version. The approximation is only on D, not on the whole interval. CW transfer check: finite-scale mass losses multiply, so their exponents add. For a discarded vertical set of length beta, the incidence mass is at most a constant times delta^2 #T beta; dividing by M=lambda delta^2 #T cancels #T. Choose beta below the current density. At the finest mesh use the identity cover; do not invoke a middle-scale statement at its excluded endpoint. Approximation remains only on the retained set D.

nodes.title: A nested trapezoid tree for the slope graph
nodes.source: WZ1: pp. 40-41; CW configuration transfer: WZ2 Sections 6.2-6.3
nodes.statement:
With the hypotheses of Lemma 5.5, a suitable $\varepsilon$-CW-extremal subcollection has trapezoid families $\mathcal R_j$ with $\rho_j=\delta^{j/N}$:
slopes lie in $[-2,2]$; height is $\rho_j$; lengths lie in $[\rho_j^{1/2+\varepsilon},\rho_j^{1/2}]$; horizontal projections are $\rho_j^{1/2}$-separated; every child has a unique containing parent; and $\operatorname{graph}(f|_D)\subset\bigcup_{R\in\mathcal R_N}R$.
nodes.note: Interface note. CW transfer check: affine interpolation extends |L_j-L_(j-1)|<=rho_j+rho_(j-1) from D to the relevant convex hull. Choose the popularity exponent much smaller than epsilon/N to obtain the claimed trapezoid length. Fixed height margins give nesting. The construction depends on the retained function graph and mass budget, not an absolute tube normalization.

nodes.title: Smooth extension of an affine segment
nodes.source: WZ1: pp. 41-42; CW configuration transfer: WZ2 Sections 6.2-6.3
nodes.statement:
For $x_1<x_2$, $a>0$ and the segment from $(x_1,y_1)$ to $(x_2,y_2)$, there is a $C^2$ function $G:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ whose graph contains that segment and which vanishes outside $[x_1-a,x_2+a]$.
With $h=|y_1|+|y_2|$ and $s=(y_2-y_1)/(x_2-x_1)$,
$|G'|\lesssim h/a+|s|$ and $|G''|\lesssim h/a^2+|s|/a$.

nodes.title: A trapezoid tree produces a C2 approximation
nodes.statement:
Let $N\ge2$ and $\eta>0$. Suppose the trapezoid families satisfy the same bounds and nesting as Corollary 5.6, with $\eta$ in place of $\varepsilon$, and $\operatorname{graph}(f|_D)$ lies in the last-level union.
Then some $C^2$ function $g$ satisfies $|f-g|\le\delta$ on $D$,
$|g''|\lesssim\delta^{-1/N-2\eta}$, and for $x\in\pi_z(R)$ with $R\in\mathcal R_j$,
$|g'(x)-\operatorname{slope}(R)|\lesssim\rho_j/\rho_{j+1}^{1/2+\eta}$.
nodes.note: Interface note. The source labels the proof 'Proof of Lemma 5.7', but the numbered statement is Proposition 5.7. The derivative comparison uses j<N; at the last level the tail of the patch sum is zero. The sketch preserves the printed [0,1] domain of the displayed second-derivative bound.

nodes.title: Global grains with a C2 slope
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF p. 40; transferred WZ1 Proposition 5.1
nodes.statement:
For every $\varepsilon,\delta_0>0$, an $\varepsilon$-extremal pair at some $0<\delta\le\delta_0$ has global grains with $\|f\|_{C^2([-1,1])}\le1$ and retains the same local grains with a $1$-Lipschitz plane map.
The WZ1 Section 5 construction uses its Section 8 dot-product projection theorem; that entire internal branch remains in this atlas.

nodes.title: A thin projection forces near orthogonality
nodes.statement:
Let $0\le\alpha<1$, $\delta\le\rho\le1$, and let $U$ be a length-$\rho^{1/2}$ segment of a $\delta$-tube $T$.
If $F\subset U$, $|F|\ge\delta^\varepsilon|U|$, and $v\cdot F$ is a $(\rho,\alpha,\delta^{-\varepsilon})_1$-ADset for a unit $v$, then
$|v\cdot\operatorname{dir}T|\lesssim\delta^{-2\varepsilon/(1-\alpha)}\rho^{1/2}$.

nodes.title: Popular grains in a thin horizontal slab
nodes.source: WZ1 pp. 44-46; summarized by WZ2 PDF pp. 41-42
nodes.statement:
Assume $|J|=\sqrt\rho$ and that $f'$ is small at a point of the popular slab.
After normalizing $f(0)=0$, bounded $f''$ gives $|f|\lesssim\rho$ on $J$.
Refine to a set $F_2$ with dense global grains, select a popular $y$-slice, and cover its $(x,z)$-projection by $\lesssim\delta^{-O(\eta)}\rho^{-1/2+\sigma/2}$ squares $S$ of side $\sqrt\rho$.
For $P_S=S\times\mathbb R_y$ the projection $(F_2\cap P_S)\cdot\widetilde V(p_S)$ is a $(\rho,1-\sigma,\delta^{-O(\eta)})_1$-ADset, where $\widetilde V=(V_x,0,V_z)$ has norm bounded below.
nodes.note: Interface note. A grouped unnumbered construction inside the old lemma, not a second invocation of its direction-separated conclusion. The local and global grain hypotheses are outputs from WZ2 Proposition 6.4.

nodes.title: Convex Wolff contradicts a popular thin slab
nodes.source: WZ2 equations (6.8)-(6.10), PDF pp. 42-43
nodes.statement:
The popular-square argument gives a family $\mathcal T_S$ with
$\#\mathcal T_S\gtrsim\delta^{O(\eta)}\rho^{(1-\sigma)/2}\#\mathcal T$.
WZ1 Lemma 6.2 makes its directions nearly orthogonal to $\widetilde V(p_S)$; since all tubes meet $P_S$, their full tubes lie in one slab $\Sigma_S$ of thickness $\delta^{-O(\eta)}\sqrt\rho$.
Convex Wolff gives $\#\mathcal T_S\lesssim\delta^{-O(\eta)}\sqrt\rho\#\mathcal T$.
Thus $\rho^{-\sigma/2}\lesssim\delta^{-O(\eta)}$, impossible when $\sqrt\rho=|J|\le\delta^\varepsilon$ and $\eta\ll\varepsilon\sigma$.
nodes.note: Interface note. This replaces the parallel-direction pigeonhole contradiction in WZ1. It uses a normalized convex slab count, so the common factor #T cancels; no separated directions or upper tube cardinality is used.

nodes.title: The slope cannot be flat on a popular slab
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF pp. 41-43; replaces WZ1 Lemma 6.3
nodes.statement:
Let $C,f,V$ satisfy Proposition 6.4 with loss $\eta$. Let $\delta^{1/2}\le|J|\le\delta^\varepsilon$.
Assume $\sum_T|Y(T)\cap(\mathbb R^2\times J)|\ge\delta^\eta|J|$ and that the shaded union in this slab is covered by at most $\delta^{-\eta}|J|^{-2+\sigma}$ cubes of side $|J|$.
For sufficiently small $\eta,\delta_0$ one has $|f'(z)|\ge|J|$ for every $z\in J$.

nodes.title: A thick slab with comparable nonzero derivative
nodes.source: WZ1 Lemma 6.4, pp. 47-48; WZ2 proof of Proposition 6.5 uses Lemma 6.6 instead of WZ1 Lemma 6.3
nodes.statement:
For every $\varepsilon,\delta_0>0$, some $0<\delta\le\delta_0$ admits a configuration satisfying Proposition 5.1 and with all shadings in $[-1,1]^2\times[0,\delta^\varepsilon]$.
There is $m\ge\delta^\varepsilon$ such that $m\le|f'(z)|\le2m$ on $[0,\delta^\varepsilon]$.
nodes.note: Interface note. Remove the initial direction-separated subcollection selection in the WZ1 proof. The popular slab is selected using the normalized coarse counts from WZ2 Proposition 6.2, and nonflatness is supplied by WZ2 Lemma 6.6. No direction selection node survives.

nodes.title: Nonsingular C2 global grains
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF pp. 41, 43; assembly from WZ1 Proposition 6.1
nodes.statement:
For every $\varepsilon,\delta_0>0$, an $\varepsilon$-extremal pair at some $0<\delta\le\delta_0$ has global grains for a $C^2$ slope satisfying
\[1\le|f'(z)|\le2,\qquad |f''(z)|\le1/100\quad(-1\le z\le1).\]
The local grains and $1$-Lipschitz plane map are retained.
Use the transferred comparable-slope slab lemma, WZ2 Lemma 6.6 and mild anisotropic normalization.

nodes.title: Extremality produces a small twisted image
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF p. 43, equation (6.11); WZ1 Corollary 6.5 ancestry
nodes.statement:
For every small loss $\varepsilon>0$ and cutoff $\delta_0>0$, obtain a convex-Wolff family with error $\delta^{-\varepsilon}$, shading density $\delta^\varepsilon$, and a nonsingular slope such that
\[|X_f(C)|\lesssim\delta^{\sigma-\varepsilon},\qquad
X_f(C)=\bigcup_T\pi_f(Y(T)).\]
Indeed, the global AD slice bound gives $\mathcal E_\delta(X_f(C)\cap\{z=t\})\le\delta^{-\varepsilon}\delta^{-(1-\sigma)}$; multiply by $O(\delta)$ and integrate in $t$.
nodes.note: Interface note. Equation (6.11) in the supplied WZ2 PDF prints sigma+epsilon. The direct consequence of the displayed AD bound is sigma-epsilon (with harmless constant losses). This weaker, explicitly derived statement is sufficient for the contradiction and is the one used in all three roadmap formats.

nodes.title: Twisted projection
nodes.source: WZ1 p. 48; WZ2 PDF p. 43
nodes.statement:
For a slope function $f$, set $\pi_f(x,y,z)=(x+yf(z),z)$.
For a line $(a,b,0)+t(c,d,1)$, its image has graph
$t\mapsto a+ct+(b+dt)f(t)$.
Global AD slice bounds and Fubini give $|\pi_f(E_C)|\lesssim\delta^{\sigma-\varepsilon}$ for the configuration from Proposition 6.1, after the usual exponent allowance.
nodes.note: Interface note. The coordinate literal is schematic for EuclideanSpace; a real implementation wraps the vector literal in the appropriate WithLp constructor.

nodes.title: The weaker radius-squared tube count
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF p. 44
nodes.statement:
The Tube Wolff axiom with error $A$ requires
$\#\mathcal T[U_r]\le Ar^2\#\mathcal T$ for every $r$-tube $U_r$, $\delta\le r\le1$.
Convex Wolff implies this condition by testing a convex tube of volume $O(r^2)$.
Section 7 needs only this weaker condition; it does not assume multi-scale convex Wolff.

nodes.title: Absolute Katz-Tao entropy bound
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF p. 44
nodes.statement:
A bounded nonempty set is $(\delta,s,C)$-Katz-Tao if
\[\mathcal E_\delta(A\cap B(x,r))\le C(r/\delta)^s,\qquad\delta\le r\le1.\]
This is an absolute count, not a normalized fraction of $\mathcal E_\delta(A)$.
For $s\le1$ it implies the one-dimensional absolute ball condition required by the cinematic maximal theorem, after parameter/jet metric comparison.
nodes.note: Interface note. The supplied PDF displays (delta/r)^s in Definition 7.2. The counting arguments, Lemma 7.11 and the standard Katz-Tao convention require (r/delta)^s. The atlas displays that corrected ratio and records the source discrepancy here.

nodes.title: Normalized Frostman entropy
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF p. 44
nodes.statement:
A bounded nonempty $A\subset\mathbb R^n$ is $(\delta,s,C)$-Frostman if
\[\mathcal E_\delta(A\cap B(x,r))\le Cr^s\mathcal E_\delta(A),\qquad\delta\le r\le1.\]
In a bounded line chart, Tube Wolff makes the parameter set
$\mathcal A=\{(a,b,c,d):\ell(t)=(a+ct,b+dt,t)\}$ a normalized $(\delta,2,O(C))$-Frostman set in $\mathbb R^4$.

nodes.title: Uniform occupied-cell counts
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF p. 45
nodes.statement:
At the prescribed sparse dyadic scales $r=2^{-j/\eta}$ between $\delta$ and $1$, the counts $\mathcal E_\delta(A\cap Q)$ in occupied $r$-cells are comparable within the fixed factor $100$.
Use a consistent grid convention (or bounded-overlap ball version).
This uniformity concerns a set's nested occupied cells, not the hypergraph uniform density used in WZ1 Section 8.

nodes.title: Cinematic families of C2 functions
nodes.statement:
A family $\mathcal F\subset C^2(I)$ is cinematic with constants $K,D$ if its diameter in the $C^2$ norm is at most $K$, it is a doubling metric space with constant $D$, and for every $g,h\in\mathcal F$,
$\inf_{t\in I}(|g-h|+|g'-h'|+|g''-h''|)(t)\ge K^{-1}\|g-h\|_{C^2(I)}$.
nodes.note: Interface note. C2Function, the jet metric, and DoublingBound are proposed project definitions. The inequality may be expressed pointwise instead of using an infimum.

nodes.title: Cinematic maximal estimate
nodes.source: WZ1 p. 49; WZ2 PDF pp. 47-48; PYZ Theorem 1.7
nodes.statement:
For a cinematic family on a compact interval and every $\varepsilon>0$, sufficiently small $\delta$ has the following property.
A $\delta$-separated finite subfamily $F$ satisfying
$\#(F\cap B)\le\delta^{-\varepsilon}(r/\delta)$ for every $C^2$-ball of diameter $r$
obeys
$\|\sum_{g\in F}1_{N_\delta(\operatorname{graph}g)}\|_{L^{3/2}}\le\delta^{-\varepsilon}$.
The small-scale threshold depends on the cinematic and doubling constants. The ball condition here is absolute one-dimensional Katz-Tao control. Relative Frostman control would instead contain $r\#G$ on the right.
nodes.note: Interface note. An imported cinematic maximal theorem. This interface is used only after extracting an absolute one-dimensional nonconcentration bound in C2 space; a two-dimensional normalized Frostman bound on R4 parameters is not a substitute.

nodes.title: The twisted-line family is cinematic
nodes.source: WZ1 Lemma 7.3, pp. 49-50; invoked in WZ2 proof of Lemma 7.12, PDF p. 49
nodes.statement:
If $f(0)=0$, $1\le|f'|\le2$ and $|f''|\le1/100$ on $[0,1]$, then
$M_f=\{g_{a,b,d}:g_{a,b,d}(t)=a+bf(t)+dtf(t),\ a,b,d\in[-1,1]\}$
is cinematic with absolute constants.
The proof compares the $C^2$ distance to the distance between parameter triples and bounds the size of the 2-jet from below at every point.
nodes.note: Interface note. Normalize the bounded t-interval and subtract f(0) if needed. A fixed c contributes the common target shear (u,t) -> (u-ct,t), or equivalently the common summand ct in every curve. Area and all pairwise jet distances are preserved.

nodes.title: Frostman sets contain large Katz-Tao subsets
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF pp. 44-45
nodes.statement:
A $(\delta,s,C)$-Frostman set has a $(\delta,s,100)$-Katz-Tao subset $A'$ with
$\mathcal E_\delta(A')\gtrsim_{n,s}\delta^{-s}|\log\delta|^{-1}C^{-1}$.
Apply the Hausdorff-content discretization after thickening to the mesh and, if necessary, pull the selected net back to $A$ with bounded losses.
nodes.note: Interface note. For a finite parameter net use delta-content, or thicken by delta before applying the ordinary content lemma. A finite set has zero ordinary positive-dimensional Hausdorff content; do not apply that continuous hypothesis directly to a finite net.

nodes.title: Sparse-scale uniform refinement
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF p. 46; WZ2 [11, Lemma 2.15]
nodes.statement:
If $\delta=2^{-T/\eta}$ and $A\subset[0,1]^n$, there is an $\eta$-uniform subset $A'$ with
$\mathcal E_\delta(A')\ge(2T)^{-1/\eta}\mathcal E_\delta(A)$.
For fixed $\eta$ this polylogarithmic loss is smaller than any reserved $\delta$-power when $\delta$ is sufficiently small.

nodes.title: Zoom to Frostman fibres of a uniform set
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF pp. 46-47
nodes.statement:
For every $\varepsilon>0$ choose $\eta>0$.
If $A\subset[0,1]^n$ is $\eta$-uniform and $\mathcal E_\delta(A)\ge\delta^{-s}$, there is $q\in(\delta^{1-\varepsilon},1]$ such that every occupied $q$-cube $Q$ has
$S_Q(A\cap Q)$ a $(\delta/q,s,(\delta/q)^{-4n\varepsilon})$-Frostman set.
The proof merges the scale profile until its exponents increase, then selects the first interval at or above $s-\varepsilon$ and absorbs that small exponent deficit into the error.
nodes.note: Interface note. Ambient dimension n replaces the inconsistent d/n notation in the source. The statements quoted from Shmerkin-Wang retain their complete quantitative contracts; only the local proof assembly is expanded.

nodes.title: Replicate a local Katz-Tao cluster
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF p. 47; density-budget version of the same proof
nodes.statement:
Let $A_0$ lie in a $q$-cube and satisfy a $(\delta,s,C)$-Katz-Tao bound.
Place $\asymp q^{-s}$ translated copies on a grid of spacing $\asymp q^{s/n}$.
The union $A^*$ is $(\delta,s,O(C))$-Katz-Tao and
$\mathcal E_\delta(A^*)\asymp q^{-s}\mathcal E_\delta(A_0)$.
If $\mathcal E_\delta(A_0)\ge\kappa(q/\delta)^s$, then $\mathcal E_\delta(A^*)\gtrsim\kappa\delta^{-s}$.
The printed lemma is the saturated case $\kappa\asymp1$.
nodes.note: Interface note. The extraction in Lemma 7.12 is only nearly saturated. Keeping kappa visible avoids using the saturated statement without its hypothesis. The upper count proof is unchanged: use one cluster below the grid spacing and the grid count above it.

nodes.title: Uniformize the projected incidence set
nodes.source: WZ2 proof of Lemma 7.12, PDF p. 48
nodes.statement:
Pigeonhole the fibre incidence multiplicity of $\pi_f$ to a dyadic level $X_\lambda$.
Apply uniform refinement to obtain an $\eta$-uniform target set $X\subset X_\lambda$ and pull it back to a sub-shading $Y'$.
The constant fibre-incidence level makes projected-area retention comparable to retained shading mass; after selecting popular tubes the shading loss is a controlled small power.

nodes.title: A rich fixed-c slice of R4 parameters
nodes.source: WZ2 Remark 7.4 and proof of Lemma 7.12, PDF pp. 44, 48
nodes.statement:
Tube Wolff gives a normalized two-dimensional Frostman bound for $\mathcal A\subset\mathbb R^4$ and hence $\mathcal E_\delta(\mathcal A)\gtrsim\delta^{-2+O(\eta)}$.
After the density and fibre refinements, some $\delta$-slab of the $c$-coordinate contains a uniformly shaded triple set $A_c\subset\mathbb R^3_{a,b,d}$ with
$\mathcal E_\delta(A_c)\gtrsim\delta^{-1+O(\eta)}$.
Freeze $c$ with an $O(\delta)$ target error and then apply a sparse-scale uniform refinement to this slice.
nodes.note: Interface note. This is a finite delta-slab pigeonhole, not an exact continuum fibre theorem. Exact c-fibres can be empty for a finite net. Shade transport and target thickening absorb the O(delta) freezing error.

nodes.title: Convert Katz-Tao triples to separated curves
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF pp. 48-49; WZ1 Lemma 7.3
nodes.statement:
Zoom the uniform triple set to a $q$-cube, extract Katz-Tao triples at $h=\delta/q$, and replicate them back at mesh $\delta$.
For fixed $c$ the functions $g(t)=a+bf(t)+dtf(t)+ct$ are cinematic; their parameter metric and $C^2$ metric are comparable.
A $(\delta,1-\tau,O(1))$-Katz-Tao parameter set therefore gives a $\delta$-separated curve family obeying
$\#(G\cap B_r)\lesssim(r/\delta)$.
All cardinality and shading deficits from extraction remain explicit small powers of $h$.

nodes.title: From cinematic norm to a local area ratio
nodes.source: WZ2 equations (7.4)-(7.6), PDF pp. 49-50
nodes.statement:
For $H=\sum_{g\in G}1_{N_{O(\delta)}(\operatorname{graph}g)}$ and the replicated shaded image $Z$, Holder gives
$M_{\rm proj}\le |Z|^{1/3}\|H\|_{3/2}$.
Here $M_{\rm proj}=\sum_T|\pi_f(Y'(T))|$ is projected area mass; a uniformly dense tube contributes $\gtrsim\lambda\delta$.
Translated parameter clusters have identical slice-image area: at time $t$ their displacement is $a_0+b_0f(t)+d_0tf(t)$.
Divide by the number of replicas to obtain an area lower bound for one cluster, relative to its $O(q)$-neighbourhood.
nodes.note: Interface note. Use a separately chosen cinematic exponent: h=delta/q lies between delta and delta^tau, so delta^(-tau^2) is at most h^(-tau). The fixed maximal-theorem constants are absorbed by another reserved margin. This prevents a delta-loss from being confused with an h-loss.

nodes.title: One-step fine-to-coarse projected-area comparison
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF pp. 47-50, equation (7.2)
nodes.statement:
For every $\varepsilon>0$ choose $\eta,\delta_0>0$.
For a Tube-Wolff family with error $\delta^{-\eta}$, $\delta^\eta$-dense shading and nonsingular slope, there are $r\in(\delta^{1-\varepsilon^2},1)$ and a sub-shading $Y'$ that is $\delta^{4\eta}$-dense such that
\[\left|\bigcup_T\pi_f(Y'(T))\right|\ge(\delta/r)^\varepsilon
\left|N_r\!\left(\bigcup_T\pi_f(Y'(T))\right)\right|.\]
The exact mesh can be rounded to the sparse scale set with bounded losses.
nodes.note: Interface note. The source states this quantitative lemma and proves it by the sliced/replicated cinematic construction. The cards separate the overloaded source scales, keep the near-saturation deficit and reserve independent small-loss budgets.

nodes.title: Uniform Tube-Wolff coarsening
nodes.source: WZ2 proof of Proposition 7.1, PDF pp. 50-51
nodes.statement:
For a uniform parameter family, choose occupied $r$-cells as parent tubes and comparable numbers of children per cell.
The normalized radius-squared Tube-Wolff count passes to this coarse family with controlled losses.
Define the coarse shading by $Y_r(U)=N_r(\bigcup_{T\in\mathcal T[U]}Y'(T))$ and retain its density and compatible target-neighbourhood bounds.
This is the coarsening operation used at every step of the projection iteration.
nodes.note: Interface note. Uniformity is applied in line-parameter space. It is required to convert normalized fine counts into normalized coarse counts; thickening without controlling child counts is insufficient.

nodes.title: Telescope the ratios up to a coarse scale
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF pp. 50-51
nodes.statement:
Let $r_0=\delta$ and apply the one-step comparison successively to uniform coarse families.
Take $r_{j+1}>r_j^{1-\theta}$ with $\theta>0$ fixed by the final error, until $r_N\ge\delta^\theta$.
One may use
$N\le 1+\lceil\log\theta/\log(1-\theta)\rceil$, a constant depending only on $\theta$.
The ratios telescope to $(\delta/r_N)^\varepsilon$; the terminal nonempty coarse curve neighbourhood has area $\gtrsim r_N$.
Choose the initial density/error budget for these finitely many calls, and rename the final exponent.
nodes.note: Interface note. The source writes N <= epsilon^(-2) and uses rho_2 in its last telescoping line. The atlas uses a valid finite iteration bound and r_N as the terminal scale; neither literal numerical slip is needed for the theorem.

nodes.title: Twisted-image lower bound under Tube Wolff
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF pp. 44, 50-51
nodes.statement:
For every $\varepsilon>0$ choose $\eta,\delta_0>0$.
For $0<\delta\le\delta_0$, Tube-Wolff error $\delta^{-\eta}$, $\delta^\eta$-dense shading and a nonsingular slope imply
$|\bigcup_T\pi_f(Y(T))|\ge\delta^\varepsilon$.
This is the stronger Section 7 statement that proves Proposition 6.8.

nodes.title: Twisted-image lower bound under convex Wolff
nodes.source: WZ2 PDF pp. 43-44; proved by Proposition 7.1
nodes.statement:
For every $\varepsilon>0$, convex-Wolff error $\delta^{-\eta}$ and $\delta^\eta$-dense shading imply
$|\bigcup_T\pi_f(Y(T))|\ge\delta^\varepsilon$ for any nonsingular $C^2$ slope and all sufficiently small $\delta$.
The required $\eta,\delta_0$ depend on $\varepsilon$.
Use convex Wolff $\Rightarrow$ Tube Wolff, then Proposition 7.1.

nodes.title: Normalized discretized Frostman sets
nodes.statement:
A $(\delta,\alpha,C)_n$-Frostman set is a union of $\delta$-cubes with
$|E\cap B(x,r)|\le Cr^\alpha |E|$ for every $r\ge\delta$.
The analogue on $S^1$ uses unions of $\delta$-arcs. Unlike Definition 4.2, this condition is normalized by $|E|$, controls balls at one discretization scale, and need not pass to subsets with the same constant.
An ADset of volume at least $c\delta^{n-\alpha}$ is Frostman with constant $C/c$.
nodes.note: Interface note. Whenever probability measures are normalized by |E|, add 0<|E| and finite measurability hypotheses. Empty sets cause vacuous alternatives rather than legitimate normalized measures. Relative Frostman convention: for equal-size occupied mesh cubes the normalized volume formulation is equivalent, up to fixed constants, to the entropy formulation in WZ2 Definition 7.3. It is not the absolute Katz-Tao condition.

nodes.title: Hypergraph fibres and uniform density
nodes.statement:
For $H\subset A_1\times\cdots\times A_k$, a coordinate subset $I$ and an edge $h$,
$n_H[h_I]=\{e\in H:e_i=h_i\ {\rm for}\ i\in I\}$.
The hypergraph is uniformly $c$-dense when
$\#n_H[h_I]\ge c\prod_{i\notin I}\#A_i$
for every $h\in H$ and every $I\subset[k]$.
For Section 8, vertices are occupied $\delta$-cells, as specified in Section 8.0.1.
nodes.note: Interface note. The product is over the unfixed coordinates i not in I. Surjective projection onto a chosen vertex class is needed for the induced-subgraph density observation in Remark 8.2.

nodes.title: Thin tubes for probability measures
nodes.statement:
Probability measures $(
u_1,
u_2)$ have $( eta,K,1-c)$-thin tubes when some Borel
$E\subset\operatorname{supp}
u_1	imes\operatorname{supp}
u_2$ has $(
u_1	imes
u_2)(E)\ge1-c$ and
$
u_2(\{b_2\in N_r(\ell):(b_1,b_2)\in E\})\le Kr^ eta$
for all $b_1\in\operatorname{supp}
u_1$, all lines $\ell$ through $b_1$, and all $r>0$.
The condition is directional: interchanging the measures is a separate hypothesis.

nodes.title: Discretized thin tubes
nodes.statement:
For unions $G_1,G_2$ of $\delta$-squares, require a product-grid set $E\subset G_1\times G_2$ with $|E|\ge(1-c)|G_1||G_2|$ and
$|\{b_2\in G_2\cap N_r(\ell):(b_1,b_2)\in E\}|\le Kr^\beta|G_2|$
for every $b_1\in G_1$, every line through $b_1$, and every $r\ge\delta$.
We write this as $\operatorname{Thin}_\delta(\beta,K,c;G_1,G_2)$, where the final argument c denotes discarded mass.

nodes.title: Standard separation
nodes.statement:
For $F,G_1,G_2\subset[0,1]^2$, standard separation means
$\operatorname{diam}F,\operatorname{diam}G_1,\operatorname{diam}G_2\le1/10$,
$\operatorname{dist}(G_1,G_2)\ge1/2$, and $\operatorname{dist}(F,0)\ge1/2$.
The final reduction removes these restrictions by localization, common translation of $G_1,G_2$, and controlled dilations.

nodes.title: Hypergraph refinement
nodes.statement:
For a finite $k$-partite hypergraph $H$ of density $d=\#H/\prod_i\#A_i$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$, there is $H'\subset H$ with
$\#H'\ge(1-\varepsilon)\#H$ that is uniformly $(2^{-k}\varepsilon d)$-dense.
The source proves the general statement by pruning all under-popular coordinate fibres.
nodes.note: Interface note. The k=2, epsilon=1/2 antecedent is attributed to [14]. The general lemma is proved inside this paper and is not an external axiom.

nodes.title: A discretized Kaufman estimate with dense fibres
nodes.statement:
For $0<\alpha\le\beta\le1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, let $F\subset\mathbb R^2$ and $\Lambda\subset S^1$ be $(\delta,\alpha,C)$- and $(\delta,\beta,C)$-Frostman sets.
If $H\subset\Lambda\times F$ has density $d=|H|/(|\Lambda||F|)$, there is $\Lambda'\subset\Lambda$ with $|\Lambda'|\gtrsim d|\Lambda|$ and, for every $\theta\in\Lambda'$,
$|\theta\cdot F_\theta|\gtrsim C^{-2}d^3\delta^{1-\alpha+\varepsilon}$, where $F_\theta=\{x:(\theta,x)\in H\}$.
nodes.note: Interface note. This version is re-proved on pp. 54-55 using energy estimates and Lemma 8.1. [24] records historical provenance rather than an unproved input to this proof.

nodes.title: Pass from measure thin tubes to grid thin tubes
nodes.statement:
Let $
u_i$ be normalized Lebesgue measures on the positive-volume grid sets $G_i$.
If $(
u_1,
u_2)$ has $( eta,K,1-c)$-thin tubes, the paper states that $(G_1,G_2)$ has $\delta$-discretized $( eta,K',1-c)$-thin tubes, with $K'=4^ eta K/c$.
This quantitative statement is recorded as printed; its use requires $c>0$.
nodes.note: Interface note. This atlas is a statement blueprint, not a verification of the measure-to-grid proof. Any quantitative implementation must check the bad-mass bookkeeping in that proof before adopting the printed constants.

nodes.title: Thin tubes force a large dot-product image
nodes.statement:
For $\varepsilon>0$, sufficiently small $\delta$, and $K\ge1$, let $F,G_1,G_2$ be $(\delta,1,K)$-Frostman sets with standard separation.
If $(G_1,G_2)$ has discretized $(1,K,1-c)$-thin tubes and $H\subset F\times G_1\times G_2$ is uniformly $2c$-dense, then
$\mathcal E_\delta(\{a\cdot(b_1-b_2):(a,b_1,b_2)\in H\})\gtrsim c^5K^{-2}\delta^{\varepsilon-1}$.
nodes.note: Interface note. Uniform 2c-density is stronger than the discarded-mass c and makes intersection with the good thin-tube pairs possible.

nodes.title: Radial bootstrap for measures
nodes.statement:
Given $\beta,\varepsilon>0$, there are $\tau=\tau(\beta,\varepsilon)>0$ and $M=M(\beta,\varepsilon)\ge1$.
Let $\beta\le s\le1-\varepsilon$, $0<c<1/10$, $K,C\ge1$, and let separated probability measures satisfy $\nu_i(B(x,r))\le Cr$.
If both ordered pairs have $(s,K,1-c)$-thin tubes, both have $(s+\tau,K',1-3c)$-thin tubes, where
$K'=\max\{K,C^2M/c\}^{M}$.
nodes.note: Interface note. s denotes the thin-tube exponent here, avoiding confusion with sigma_3. The paper explains its compact-range uniformity and the freedom in beta in Remark 8.4; it ultimately fixes beta=1/4.

nodes.title: Radial bootstrap for grid sets
nodes.statement:
Fix $\beta=1/4$. The same conclusion holds for separated $(\delta,1,C)$-Frostman grid sets and both ordered discretized thin-tube pairs with exponent $s\in[1/4,1-\varepsilon]$.
The resulting exponent is $s+\tau$, discarded mass is $3c$, and
$K'=\max\{4K/(3c),\,4C^2M/(3c^2)\}^{M}$.

nodes.title: Iterate the bootstrap up to exponent 1
nodes.statement:
For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $N=N(\varepsilon)\ge1$.
If both ordered pairs of separated $(\delta,1,C)$-Frostman sets have discretized $(1/4,K,1-c)$-thin tubes, both have exponent $1-\varepsilon$, constant
$K'=\max\{4K/(3c),4C^2N/(3c^2)\}^{N}$, and discarded mass $3^Nc$.
At scales $r\ge\delta$, these are also exponent-1 thin tubes with constant $\delta^{-\varepsilon}K'$.
nodes.note: Interface note. The term 3^N c is a power, not 3Nc. If it reaches 1, the probability-mass conclusion must be treated as vacuous or the initial c must be chosen smaller; the application does choose c sufficiently small.

nodes.title: Obtain a fixed 1/4-thin-tube seed
nodes.statement:
For $\lambda,\zeta,\alpha>0$ and sufficiently small $\delta$, let separated $G_1,G_2$ be $(\delta,1,\delta^{-\lambda})$-Frostman sets.
If $|G_2\cap N_r(\ell)|\le(\delta^{-\lambda}r)^\zeta |G_2|$ for all lines and $r\ge\delta$, then
$(G_1,G_2)$ has discretized $(1/4,\delta^{-3\alpha/\zeta-\lambda},1-\delta^\alpha)$-thin tubes.
Swapping the roles gives the reverse ordered pair when both sets satisfy the strip bound.
nodes.note: Interface note. The fixed seed exponent is important: starting the iteration directly at zeta would make lambda depend on zeta, contrary to the quantifier contract of Proposition 8.5 (Remark 8.5).

nodes.title: Strip nonconcentration forces expansion
nodes.statement:
For $0<\varepsilon,\zeta<1$, choose $\lambda=\lambda(\varepsilon)>0$, $\alpha=\alpha(\varepsilon,\zeta)>0$ and $\delta_0$.
Let $F,G_1,G_2$ be $(\delta,1,\delta^{-\lambda})$-Frostman sets with standard separation. Require
$|G_i\cap N_r(\ell)|\le(\delta^{-\lambda}r)^\zeta|G_i|$ for all lines and $r\ge\delta$.
For uniformly $\delta^\alpha$-dense $H$,
$\mathcal E_\delta(\{a\cdot(b_1-b_2):(a,b_1,b_2)\in H\})\ge\delta^{\varepsilon-1}$.
nodes.note: Interface note. Lambda is chosen before zeta. This dependency matters in the anisotropic reduction and must not be weakened in a Lean interface.

nodes.title: Two-ends localization to a strip
nodes.statement:
For a $\delta$-square union $E\subset[0,1]^2$ and $0<\zeta\le1/4$, some width $w>0$ and line $\ell$ give $E'=E\cap N_w(\ell)$ with
$|E'|\ge\tfrac12w^\zeta |E|$ and
$|E'\cap N_r(\ell')|\le(r/w)^\zeta|E'|$
for every line $\ell'$ and every $0<r\le1$.
nodes.note: Interface note. The paper calls this standard and omits the proof. It still needs an implementation; it is not an external citation.

nodes.title: Restore Frostman after anisotropic rescaling
nodes.statement:
For $\varepsilon>0$, sufficiently small $\delta$, $w\in[\delta^{1-\varepsilon},1]$, a $1\times w$ rectangle $R$, a $(\delta,1,C)$-Frostman set $E\subset R$, and the affine map $\phi:R\to[0,1]^2$:
some $E'\subset E$ has $|E'|\ge(\delta/w)^\varepsilon|E|$ such that the union of $\delta/w$-squares meeting $\phi(E')$ is $(\delta/w,1,(w/\delta)^\varepsilon C)$-Frostman.
Each occupied output square has comparable intersection volume with $\phi(E')$.
nodes.note: Interface note. Normalized Frostman constants are not inherited unchanged by arbitrary refinement. The occupancy condition is precisely what makes this transport estimate work.

nodes.title: Frostman coarsening after pigeonholing
nodes.statement: For $0<\delta\le\rho\le1$ and a $(\delta,\alpha,C)$-Frostman set $E\subset\mathbb R^2$, there is $E'\subset E$ with $|E'|\ge|\log\delta|^{-1}|E|$ such that the union of $\rho$-squares meeting $E'$ is $(\rho,\alpha,C')$-Frostman, with $C'\asymp|\log\delta|C$.
nodes.note: Interface note. The printed formula is meaningful only below scale 1. In applications delta is sufficiently small and all logarithmic factors are absorbed into power allowances.

nodes.title: Comparable orthogonal strips or expansion
nodes.statement:
For sufficiently small $\delta$ and separated $(\delta,1,\delta^{-\eta})$-Frostman $F,G_1,G_2$, let $H$ be uniformly $\delta^\eta$-dense and suppose $G_1\subset N_w(\ell)$.
Either
$\pi_{G_2}H\subset N_{\delta^{-\varepsilon}w}(\ell)$ and
$\pi_FH\subset N_{\delta^{-\varepsilon}w}(\ell^\perp)$,
where $\ell^\perp$ passes through the origin; or the expansion conclusion (8.3) holds at some $\rho\ge\delta$.

nodes.title: Separated, uniform version of the dichotomy
nodes.source: WZ1: p. 61; proof pp. 66-67
nodes.statement:
For each $\varepsilon>0$, choose $\eta,\delta_0>0$.
If $F,G_1,G_2$ are $(\delta,1,\delta^{-\eta})$-Frostman sets with standard separation and $H\subset F\times G_1\times G_2$ is uniformly $\delta^\eta$-dense, either the three orthogonal-line concentration bounds (8.2) hold, or the expansion conclusion (8.3) holds for this $H$.
nodes.note: Interface note. The proof localizes to strips, compares widths, uses dual affine changes for F and the G sets, restores Frostman constants, and applies Proposition 8.5.

nodes.title: Frostman form, without separation or uniformity
nodes.source: WZ1: pp. 51-52; proof pp. 68-69
nodes.statement:
For every $\varepsilon>0$, choose $\eta,\delta_0>0$.
For $(\delta,1,\delta^{-\eta})$-Frostman $F,G_1,G_2\subset[0,1]^2$, either an affine line $\ell$ and its origin-based perpendicular satisfy
$\mathcal E_\delta(F\cap N_\delta\ell),\mathcal E_\delta(G_i\cap N_\delta\ell^\perp)\ge\delta^{\varepsilon-1}$ for $i=1,2$; or
every $H\subset F\times G_1\times G_2$ with $\mathcal E_\delta(H)\ge\delta^{\eta-3}$ satisfies the multiscale expansion conclusion (8.3).
nodes.note: Interface note. The edge to Theorem 5.2 includes the small-set/vacuous-expansion case on p. 52. AD-to-Frostman conversion alone is insufficient without a lower size bound.

nodes.title: Endpoint multilinear Kakeya
nodes.source: WZ1: Direct use: Theorem 4.2, p. 19; bibliography pp. 69-70
nodes.statement:
Imported interface: the determinant-weighted trilinear tube integral is bounded by $(\delta^2\#\mathcal T)^{3/2}$, as recorded in Theorem 4.2.
The paper credits Bennett--Carbery--Tao [1], and points to the endpoint version of Carbery--Valdimarsson [8].
nodes.note: Interface note. Black-box import. No claim is made about its current formalization status.

nodes.title: Scalar Lipschitz extension
nodes.source: WZ1: Direct use: proof of Proposition 4.1, p. 31
nodes.statement:
A real-valued $K$-Lipschitz function defined on a subset of a metric space extends to a $K$-Lipschitz function on the whole space.
Only the scalar extension of the slope $f$ is needed at this citation site. The paper cites Kirszbraun [29]; the scalar interface is already provided by Mathlib.
nodes.note: Interface note. This is a support-library fact, not an additional analytic axiom. For a Euclidean-valued extension with the Euclidean norm, use the actual Hilbert-space extension theorem rather than a sup-norm product extension.

nodes.title: Radial thin-tube bootstrap
nodes.source: WZ1: Direct use: Proposition 8.6, pp. 57-58; bibliography p. 71
nodes.statement:
Imported interface: improve the thin-tube exponent by a fixed positive amount on a compact subrange below 1, for separated 1-Frostman probability measures, with quantitative loss in the thin-tube constant and good-pair mass.
The exact specialized statement is Proposition 8.6. Source: Orponen--Shmerkin--Wang [35, Lemma 2.9].
nodes.note: Interface note. The paper's Remark 8.4 discusses how its stated interface differs from the cited lemma. That explanation is part of the import boundary.

nodes.title: Cinematic maximal: absolute Katz-Tao input
nodes.source: WZ1 [36, Theorem 1.7] = WZ2 [13, Theorem 1.7]; cinematic definition [36, Definition 1.6]
nodes.statement:
The imported cinematic maximal interface uses a $\delta$-separated subfamily $G$ of a uniformly cinematic, doubling $C^2$ family, with the absolute one-dimensional Katz-Tao count
\[\#(G\cap B_r)\le A(r/\delta).\]
It yields the $L^{3/2}$ curve-neighbourhood estimate on the Theorem 7.2 card (WZ2: Theorem 7.13). The admissible absolute constant and small-scale threshold follow that imported contract.
nodes.note: Interface note. Terminology: the source calls this a Frostman non-concentration condition, but its displayed count is absolute. Under the conventions of this atlas it is Katz-Tao, consistent with WZ2 Definition 7.2. A relative Frostman bound C*r*#G alone does not provide this interface unless an upper cardinality bound is supplied. The cited paper remains an external black box.

nodes.title: Content-to-Katz-Tao extraction
nodes.source: WZ2 Lemma 7.7, PDF p. 45; WZ2 [3, Lemma 3.13]
nodes.statement:
If the $s$-dimensional Hausdorff content of a bounded set is $\kappa>0$, then at mesh $\delta$ it contains a $(\delta,s,O(1))$-Katz-Tao set with covering number $\gtrsim\kappa\delta^{-s}$.
The fixed constant may be taken as $100$ in the WZ2 normalization.

nodes.title: Uniform refinement black box
nodes.source: WZ2 [11, Lemma 2.15], cited as WZ2 Lemma 7.9
nodes.statement:
A set at a prescribed sparse dyadic mesh admits a uniform occupied-cell refinement with the polylogarithmic loss stated in WZ2 Lemma 7.9.
No further proof from the cited paper is opened here.

nodes.title: Decompose the scale-entropy profile
nodes.source: WZ2 [14, Lemma 5.21]; WZ2 proof of Lemma 7.10, PDF p. 46
nodes.statement:
For a uniform set, decompose the scale range into finitely many intervals $[a_j,a_{j+1}]$ of a fixed minimum length, with per-interval Frostman exponents $t_j$ and weighted entropy
$\sum_jt_j(a_{j+1}-a_j)\ge s-o(1)$.
The quoted quantitative decomposition is used as a black box.

nodes.title: Merge adjacent entropy intervals
nodes.source: WZ2 [14, Lemma 5.20]; WZ2 proof of Lemma 7.10, PDF p. 46
nodes.statement:
Adjacent intervals with $t_j\ge t_{j+1}$ can be merged; their new exponent is the length-weighted average and their Frostman loss remains controlled.
The weighted entropy and the total scale length are preserved.

nodes.title: Lines, tubes, cubes, shadings
nodes.source: WZ2 Section 6.1, PDF pp. 37-38; WZ1 Section 2.1
nodes.statement:
Work in a bounded affine-line chart in $\mathbb R^3$. Throughout the structural proof, a tube is
$T_\delta(\ell)=N_{6\delta}(\ell)\cap[-1,1]^3$ and $Y(T)\subset T$ is a union of axis-aligned $\delta$-cubes.
Put $E_C=\bigcup_TY(T)$ and $\mathcal T_C(p)=\{T:p\in Y(T)\}$.
The original unit-segment tubes and measurable shadings are converted by the bounded-loss cubulation in WZ2 Section 6.1.
nodes.note: Interface note. WZ2 Section 6.1 expressly adopts the WZ1 tube and cube conventions. A finite chart split and bounded dilations are infrastructure, not a direction-separation assumption. The threshold condition for cubulation is interpreted as a cell-density condition; harmless constants are absorbed before the final scale choice.

nodes.title: Finite covering numbers
nodes.source: WZ2 Section 6.1 and Definitions 7.2-7.3; WZ1 Section 8
nodes.statement:
$\mathcal E_r(S)$ denotes the covering number of $S$ at radius/mesh $r$.
For bounded grid sets, covering numbers, separated-point counts and occupied-cube counts agree up to dimensional constants. Fix one convention and prove comparison lemmas. Neighbourhoods are $N_r(S)=\{x:\operatorname{dist}(x,S)<r\}$.
nodes.note: Interface note. CoverNum is a proposed project definition, not an assertion about an existing Mathlib declaration. Use Nat counts with explicit real coercions in inequalities.

nodes.title: Mass and constant multiplicity
nodes.source: WZ2 Definition 2.1 and Section 6.1, PDF pp. 6, 37-38
nodes.statement:
Write $m(C)=\sum_T|Y(T)|$ and $v(C)=\sum_T|T|\asymp\delta^2\#\mathcal T$.
A $\lambda$-dense shading means $m(C)\ge\lambda v(C)$; uniformly dense means $|Y(T)|\ge\lambda|T|$ for every tube.
A refinement retains $m(C')\gtrsim |\log\delta|^{-A}m(C)$. Constant-multiplicity pigeonholing gives $\sum_T1_{Y'(T)}=\mu 1_{E_{C'}}$.
Power-loss selections are separately recorded as subcollections with explicit mass retention.
nodes.note: Interface note. Average density is the hypothesis of Theorem 5.2. Uniform density is obtained by selecting popular tubes and then rebuilding the required covers; it is not silently assumed at the root.

nodes.title: Balanced coarse/fine configurations
nodes.source: WZ2 Definitions 2.10-2.12 and Section 6.1, PDF pp. 8-9, 37-38
nodes.statement:
For geometric covers, $\mathcal B[A]=\{B\in\mathcal B:B\subset A\}$.
A $K$-uniform cover has child counts comparable within $K$. A partitioning cover has disjoint families $\mathcal B[2A]$ for distinct parents.
For the shaded structural argument, use the compatible line-metric cover and require child shadings to lie in the parent shading.
A balanced cover has $|E_C\cap Q|$ independent of the occupied coarse cube $Q$; constant-multiplicity data transfers mass through such a cover. The balanced union-volume identity is $|E_{\rm fine}\cap Q|=\rho^3|E_{\rm fine}|/|E_{\rm coarse}|$. To pull back a coarse incidence selection, also pigeonhole the weights $w(U,Q)=\sum_{T\in\mathcal T[U]}|Y(T)\cap Q|$ to comparable values; volume balance alone does not supply that mass-transfer identity.
nodes.note: Interface note. Geometric partitioning, uniform child counts and balanced shaded volumes are three different requirements. WZ2 Section 6.1 reconciles the stronger WZ1 line-metric cover with geometric containment; do not identify them by definition.

nodes.title: Jacobian, direction and grid transport
nodes.source: WZ2 Section 6.1 and the transferred WZ1 Lemma 3.5; WZ1 pp. 12-14, 18
nodes.statement:
For an invertible affine map $\phi(x)=Ax+b$, volume transforms by $|\phi(S)|=|\det A|\,|S|$.
Lines and their directions are transported by $\phi$ and $v\mapsto Av/|Av|$. Projection normals are transported using the inverse transpose.
After transport, re-cubulate at the chosen scale; prove bounded overlap and containment before replacing geometric sets by grid unions.
nodes.note: Interface note. Convex-containment counts transport by the determinant and parent-volume normalization. Re-cubulation and balancing still require witnesses; no arbitrary-subcollection preservation of the multi-scale axiom is asserted.

nodes.title: C2 bounds and compactly supported patches
nodes.source: WZ1: Sections 5.2 and 7, pp. 41-50
nodes.statement:
Represent a function on a compact interval by an ambient function with a $C^2$ extension to a neighbourhood. Use the jet norm $\|f\|_{C^2(I)}=\max_{0\le j\le2}\sup_{t\in I}|f^{(j)}(t)|$.
Finite sums of patches with disjoint support at each scale preserve derivative bounds. Endpoint conventions must be fixed for derivatives and gluing.
nodes.note: Interface note. A custom normed C2 function space or a jet-based metric is needed for Definition 7.1. The signatures below use this proposed API.

nodes.title: Small-parameter and finite-iteration contracts
nodes.source: WZ2 Proposition 6.2, Lemma 7.12 and proof of Proposition 7.1; transferred WZ1 iterations
nodes.statement:
Choose $\varepsilon$ first, then all auxiliary loss exponents, and finally $\delta_0$.
At a middle scale $s$ with $\delta^a\le s\le\delta^b$, convert an error $\delta^{-\eta}$ to an $s$-error using the appropriate endpoint exponent.
For a fixed finite iteration, reserve enough loss at every call, including density, cover rebuilding and logarithmic refinements.
In Section 7, write $q$ for the parameter cube size, $h=\delta/q$ for its rescaled mesh, and $r=q$ for the final coarse spatial scale.
nodes.note: Interface note. The source repeatedly reuses rho for a cube size and a rescaled mesh. This atlas keeps them separate and uses independent cinematic and geometric loss exponents.

nodes.title: Restriction and rebuilding of cover witnesses
nodes.source: WZ2 proof of Proposition 6.2, PDF pp. 39-40
nodes.statement:
A $q$-fraction subfamily inherits a single-scale convex count with error at most $A/q$.
For the multi-scale condition, separately rebalance the partitioning tree and each surviving child fibre.
Record uniform parent counts, surviving child counts and the new errors as witnesses.
This proof operation is used for the specific refinements constructed in the argument; it is not an arbitrary-subfamily inheritance theorem.
nodes.note: Interface note. This card makes the inheritance obligation visible. The WZ2 sketch describes repeated pigeonholing to restore the axiom; a full formalization must implement that construction, not assume closure under all refinements.

nodes.title: Uniform lower envelope for admissible unions
nodes.source: WZ2 deficit definition and proof of Proposition 6.2
nodes.statement:
For every $\gamma>0$ there are $\eta,\delta_0>0$ such that every admissible pair at $0<\delta\le\delta_0$ satisfies $|E_C|\ge\delta^{\sigma+\gamma}$.
Otherwise $\sigma+\gamma$ would be a bad exponent, contradicting the supremum.
At constant multiplicity this gives $\mu\lesssim\delta^{2-\sigma-\gamma}\#\mathcal T$.
This normalized estimate replaces the old absolute multiplicity bounds.
